alternatives.title: A reconstruction isn't always a replacement.
alternatives.text: Open source does not guarantee a drop-in replacement. Early and alpha projects are welcome, with their current gaps disclosed. Some engines still need original software, assets or hardware. Check the limits before relying on a project.
start.text1: REA connects a coding agent to inspection tools through MCP or the command line. It returns findings with evidence; your agent can investigate further, explain the behavior, or write and test code.
start.text2: Native analysis uses a supported engine such as Ghidra, Hopper or IDA. Requirements vary by target. Analysis runs locally, but your coding agent's model provider may receive tool results.

faq.a1: REA is an open-source CLI and MCP server that connects coding agents to software-analysis tools. It helps investigate native binaries, JavaScript and Electron applications, and other targets. The agent uses the findings to explain behavior or develop an implementation.
faq.q2: Does REA turn any paid app into a free clone?
faq.a2: No. REA returns analysis and evidence, not a guarantee of original source recovery, full feature parity, or permission to redistribute software. A small reconstruction and a complete replacement are very different things.
faq.q3: Must a project use REA to be included?
faq.a3: No. Open-source reverse-engineering projects, independent reimplementations and compatibility layers are welcome, whether or not they use REA. We also cover REA tools and resources. Any claimed REA involvement is documented separately; source review does not establish whole-project provenance or full feature parity.
faq.q4: Is REA the same as Ghidra?
faq.a4: No. Ghidra is one of the analysis engines REA can use. REA connects engines and workflows to agents through MCP and the CLI. Native analysis needs a supported provider; static JavaScript inspection does not require a native engine.
faq.q5: Is this the official REA website?
faq.a5: No. Awesome REA is an independent curated index. The upstream repository is github.com/morluto/rea, the package is rea-agents, and the official website is rea.tools.
faq.q6: How can I submit a project or request a correction?
faq.a6: Open a project suggestion or correction Issue on GitHub. The forms ask for evidence, licensing and limitations. English or Chinese is welcome. You can also propose a data PR; every contribution is reviewed before publication.
contribute.title: Know a useful reverse-engineering project?
contribute.text: Share an open-source reconstruction, compatibility project, tool or resource with primary evidence. REA usage is not required; every submission is reviewed.
method.lead: Awesome REA helps you find open-source reverse-engineering projects, independent reimplementations and compatibility layers. REA usage is optional, not a requirement.
method.checked1: We reviewed the linked primary sources on the date shown. We checked whether the published source supports the stated project scope, license note and any claimed REA involvement. We did not independently build, execute, benchmark or security-audit the listed software.
method.checked2: Project progress and test results are author-reported unless explicitly stated otherwise. “Checked” is a source-review date, not a freshness guarantee. Pinned GitHub links preserve the reviewed snapshot where practical; project links go to current repositories.
method.relationshipsTitle: Different project relationships, not one blanket claim
method.relationship1: A separately implemented application or engine recreates documented formats, behavior or workflows. REA involvement is not required or implied; any clean-room claim remains the author's, not our legal certification.
method.relationship2: A compatibility layer or interpreter enables existing programs or data to work in another environment. It may still require original software, data or a license.
method.relationship3: The original toolkit maintained at morluto/rea.
method.relationship4: A primary project source explicitly describes how REA contributed. That credit applies only to the documented work, not automatically to every feature or prior release.
method.relationship5: The official REA site documents a specific investigation or reconstruction. A linked full project may be much broader than the demonstrated REA work.
method.relationship6: A repository contains explicit REA scripts or workflow documentation. This is a useful ecosystem connection, but is not proof that its whole product was built with REA.
method.relationship7: A plugin, skill, bridge or package explicitly integrates or distributes REA. This does not make it official or security-audited.
method.relationship8: A substantive guide, lab or resource list explicitly covers REA. Merely featuring REA is not proof of using it to build software.
method.taxonomyTitle: Purpose, type and status are separate
method.taxonomy1: Purpose groups describe what an entry is for: developer and security tools; games and engines; desktop and productivity; audio and hardware; integrations and packaging; or learning and resources. Empty groups stay hidden.
method.taxonomy2: Type describes what you get: an analysis tool, reconstruction, interoperability project, integration, case study or learning resource. The status and limitations describe maturity separately. A game reconstruction with REA tooling present is not relabeled as a verified REA-built game.
method.taxonomy3: The README directory and website are generated from one shared catalog and reviewed translations. Correct the source and translations together; regenerate both language versions.
method.inclusion1: Open-source reverse-engineering projects, independent reimplementations and compatibility tools qualify without using REA. We also include relevant tools, integrations and public learning resources. Software needs an applicable open-source license and primary evidence of its stated scope. Early and alpha work is welcome with honest limits.
method.inclusion2: Inclusion is not a full-replacement claim. That stronger claim would need a documented usable build and enough supported functionality for the particular workflow. Required original software, assets and hardware must be disclosed. We do not convert author-reported menu coverage or benchmarks into independent verification.
method.inclusion3: We exclude unexplained mirrors, download promotions, generic alternatives without evidence of the claimed reconstruction or compatibility scope, and entries we cannot describe accurately. Restrictive source-available terms are not automatically open source. This directory is curated, not an exhaustive inventory.
method.rights1: Listing a project is not legal review or endorsement. Reverse-engineering, interoperability and redistribution rules vary by jurisdiction, license agreement and terms of service. A repository's license may cover only its authors' own code — not the original software, trademarks, assets or data.
method.rights2: REA's MIT license covers REA itself, not everything analyzed with it. Use only targets you are authorized to inspect. We do not host third-party binaries, playable game data, proprietary code or instructions to bypass access controls. Small README image previews are attributed to their upstream sources; they retain their owners' rights and are not relicensed under this directory's MIT license. A preview is not evidence of a working replacement. Descriptions of “clean-room” work remain the projects' claims, not a legal certification by this index.
method.rights3: License labels summarize the reviewed notices. Per-file and third-party terms may differ. Follow the source license link before reuse. This is not legal advice.
method.corrections1: This index is maintained by Jeff Xun. Submit a project suggestion, correction / removal request, or website bug report. The forms accept English or Chinese. Experienced contributors can submit a PR following the contribution guide.
method.corrections2: Provide primary evidence, the applicable license, current limitations and any affiliation. Maintainers review a submission before merging data changes; neither an Issue nor a passing automated check publishes it. We do not automatically run submitted software. GitHub Issues are public: never submit credentials, private binaries or proprietary investigation data. For a sensitive removal request, contact the maintainer through their public GitHub profile instead.

analytics.text: Google Analytics loads only if you allow it. It uses cookies to measure page visits, without sending search terms. Declining does not affect the directory.

method.privacy1: This static site has no accounts, ads, third-party fonts or externally loaded media. README previews are optimized static images served by this site, not requests to GitHub or third-party image hosts. Search and filtering stay in your browser; search terms are not sent to us. Optional Google Analytics 4 loads only after you allow statistics on awesomerea.com. It measures page visits and basic device information using cookies; page queries and fragments are excluded, and external referrers are limited to their origin. Advertising signals and enhanced measurement are disabled. Browser Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control signals prevent collection. Your allow/decline choice is stored locally for up to 180 days; analytics cookies expire within 180 days. The footer settings let you decline or withdraw without interrupting browsing. Withdrawal stops further GA collection and clears this integration's GA cookies, but cannot recall requests already sent or delete historical data. On the production origin only, Microsoft Clarity (project yy4tlvmg63) also loads to capture anonymized session heatmaps and recordings for UX improvement, and Umami (website 47d78379-0c7b-4149-b17e-9535a292bdb8 at analytics.murdoku.fans) loads for privacy-friendly page analytics; both are separate from the GA consent choice and do not run on local or preview sites. Language preference is not stored.
method.privacy2: Cloudflare serves the site and may process request information for delivery and security. Outbound links and GitHub Issues use the destination service's privacy rules; Issue submissions are public. We do not control those services.
method.privacy3: Awesome REA is not affiliated with or endorsed by morluto, REA, or any listed project. No paid placements are included in this edition.
